messages:
pagerduty-bot: Pager duty alert: High 502/504 error rate from api-gateway-edge in us-west-2. Threshold: 20% over 5m. Investigate.
alyssa: Seeing it in dashboards now — 30% 502s on the /v1/generate route, latency spike too. Any recent deploys?
jordan: No deploys for that service in last 2 hours. I can join. Paging SRE-oncall.
sre-oncall: I'm on it. Starting root-cause triage. Can someone post recent error logs and any gateway autoscale events?
mike: Attaching recent nginx error tail from the edge LB:
```
[error] 2026/03/14 14:12:05 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream
[error] 2026/03/14 14:12:12 connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream
[error] 2026/03/14 14:12:27 upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream
```
alyssa: Upstream being our api-gateway-backend pool. I see a handful of backend nodes at 100% CPU in cloud metrics.
jordan: Can we confirm whether it's a backend saturation or network flakiness at the edge? Any recent routing changes or WAF rules?
sre-oncall: No routing or WAF changes in last 24h. Correlating logs: the 502s cluster around certain clients — looks like bursty requests from a small set of IPs that correspond to a handful of high-throughput customers.
support-lead: I'm watching customer tickets. Two customers (acct-id: C-3492, C-8810) report timeouts starting ~14:08. Escalating to enterprise CS.
alyssa: Quick mitigation idea: enable stricter per-IP rate limiting at the edge for the top offending IPs, and failover traffic to secondary gateway region for production routes if possible. Thoughts?
jordan: Rate-limit sounds low risk and can reduce upstream pressure immediately. How fast can we flip it?
sre-oncall: I can add a temporary 1000r/s cap per IP for the three offending IPs and set a 10s penalty window. Pushing in 30s. If we see improvement, we keep and refine.
pagerduty-bot: Action: sre-oncall assigned to incident (priority P1).
(30s later)
sre-oncall: Applied per-IP throttling rules on edge LB for IPs: 52.11.122.4, 18.23.9.77, 204.45.12.1. Monitoring.
mike: After throttle, backend CPU dropped from 98% to ~70% within 60s. 502 rate decreased to ~12% and falling. Latency improved.
alyssa: Good. Can we also temporarily increase backend pool by +3 instances to handle tail? Autoscaler seems slow to react because of sustained CPU threshold config.
sre-oncall: Requesting manual scale now. Hitting scale API… scaled api-gateway-backend from 6 -> 9 nodes. New capacity healthy.
jordan: Any errors in the new nodes joining?
mike: New nodes connected, but one node had init container fail once — restarted and joined successfully. No longer erroring.
support-lead: Updating affected customers: telling them we have throttled excessive clients and added capacity; monitoring for continued errors.
alyssa: Let's also enable a temporary route fallback: if gateway returns 502/504 within 200ms of request start, edge should retry once to a different backend IP (with jitter). This will smooth transient failures.
sre-oncall: Edge supports 502->retry policy — enabling with max 1 retry and 100ms jitter for /v1/* routes. Deploying now.
(60s later)
sre-oncall: Retry policy active. Observed 502->retry success rate ~30% of the prior errors. Combined with throttles and scale, 502s down to 3% in last 2m.
jordan: Great. Root cause summary so far: sudden high-throughput traffic from a few customers saturated backend pool causing connection resets/timeouts. Edge had no automatic per-IP throttle aggressive enough. Autoscaler reaction lagged.
alyssa: Long-term mitigations: 1) tighten per-IP defaults, 2) make autoscaler more responsive for burst metrics (consider burst buffer or predictive scale), 3) add dynamic circuit breaker per-route, 4) playbook update for immediate steps.
sre-oncall: Agree. I'll open a follow-up RFC for autoscale tuning and update the incident runbook.
support-lead: CS requests an incident summary for customers and a timeline. I'll draft and circulate for legal/ops review.
pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged resolved? Monitoring for 30m before close.
sre-oncall: Marking mitigation stable. Continue watch. If error rate remains below 5% for 30m, we will close.
mike: Adding logs and key metrics to the incident ticket: 14:08 — spike start; 14:12 — throttle applied; 14:14 — scale +3 nodes; 14:16 — retries enabled; 14:18 — error rate down to 3%.
alyssa: Thanks team. After-watch: rotate handoff to next oncall at 15:00. @jordan can you take the 15–17 shift and keep an eye on related customer tickets?
jordan: Yep, I'll take handoff and follow up with CS.
sre-oncall: Handing off monitoring to jordan. Leaving temporary throttles until noon tomorrow unless we get pushback from CS.
support-lead: Noted. I'm gathering the customer impact matrix and will attach in the incident ticket.
alyssa: Postmortem owner: jordan. Please include timeline, mitigations, and action items assigned.
jordan: Will do. Closing thread to further replies; will update with the postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:
